Jonas — thanks for the draft. We reviewed with Procurement and our outside counsel. High-level: we can accept the capacity bridge but need explicit language limiting Redwood's liability on data residency during pilot (Section 7.x), and we want a pro-rated termination right tied to a commercial milestone at month 6. I've attached a PDF with inline comments (Zephyrus_MSA_comments_20281123.pdf).

Key asks:
- Add a paragraph to Exhibit B clarifying KV-cache retention periods for pilot tokens.
- Remove the surge buffer clause as written; propose a hard cap of +15% on token throughput for burst months rather than open-ended surge language.
- Insert an audit notice window of 30 days for compliance evidence requests.

Our counsel (Matt Reed) suggested alternative indemnity language in the attached. If Redwood can accept the liability carve and the pro-rate termination linkage to performance, Procurement expects green light for signature.

Best,
Sophie
Head of Cloud Procurement
Zephyrus Analytics

Markus / Priyom — forwarding Zephyrus' redlines and their counsel's notes. Highlights to review for legal ops: liability carve for data residency during pilot, proposed pro-rated termination tied to "production readiness" milestone at month 6, and a requested change to the surge buffer (hard cap +15%). Also they want KV-cache retention defined in Exhibit B and a 30-day audit notice window.

Can you please:
1) Confirm whether the proposed liability carve is acceptable or a counter we should present.
2) Draft suggested language that preserves our SLO protections while addressing their data residency ask.
3) Confirm whether the +15% hard cap on burst is operationally feasible without an uptick surcharge, else propose alternative commercial language.

Timing: Procurement here is targeting signature next week; Sophie needs our counter by EOD today to stay on that cadence. If you need a quick call I can hop on at 12:00 PT.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal: term rebalance & capacity addendum - redline coordination

Team — reviewed the attached comments. Summary and proposed path: we can accept a narrow liability carve limited strictly to the pilot period (define pilot as months 0–3 and limit carve to data residency obligations only). I drafted phrasing to add to Section 7.3 in the attached (Redwood_MSA_v3-redline.pdf). We should not accept an open pro-rated termination without guardrails; counter with a termination-for-convenience at month 6 with 30 days' notice and a milestone-based credit if production readiness is not achieved (credit formula included).

On surge: operationally we can support a +15% soft cap for burst if there is an automatic buffer charge for usage beyond that cap (tiered at 15% and 30%). I suggested language for Exhibit C to make the surcharge explicit. For Exhibit B KV-cache retention, accept defining retention to 14 days for pilot tokens with an option to extend on agreement. Audit window: 30 days is fine but add an SLA for scheduling and redaction requirements.

Action items:
- Jonas: send Zephyrus our counter with the liability carve language and the termination-for-convenience + credit formula.
- Priyom: please update the order form to reflect the tiered burst pricing and the 14-day KV-cache retention default.
- Laura: loop in Sales Ops to prepare revised DocuSign packet (link below).

I'll attach the marked MSA with our language; if Sophie wants a quick call we can do 12:30 PT.

-Markus Klein
